request.prompt:
You are extracting the numeric claims of one section of a model-validation report, so that each
can be checked against the artifact it cites. Section: sensitivity.

The prose is printed below one line per line, each prefixed with its own number and a vertical
bar. List EVERY number that appears in the prose, in the order it appears, including numbers that
appear inside a citation's logical name and numbers written with a thousands separator or a per
cent sign. For each one:

- "line" is the number printed to the left of the line the number appears on. Give the number
  only; do not copy the line's text back, and do not count the prefix itself as a number.
- "value" is the number as written, with thousands separators and the per cent sign removed:
  "3,500" is 3500, "22.0%" is 22.0.
- "unit" is "percent" when the number is written with a per cent sign, "count" for a number of
  rows, features or events, "currency", "bp" for basis points, "months" for a horizon, and
  "ratio" for every other dimensionless quantity (AUC, PSI, VIF, a coefficient, a lift).
- "metric" is what the number measures, taken from the logical name of the artifact it cites
  (auc, brier, psi, vif, calibration_slope, delta_auc, coefficient, event_rate, ...), or null.
- "split" is train, test, out_of_time or vintage_holdout, or null.
- "comparison" is "eq" for a number that equals its artifact; "delta" for a difference written
  "from a to b" or "a gap of x", whose value is the second cited artifact minus the first; and
  "ratio" for a number written as one artifact divided by another. A delta or ratio carries TWO
  adjacent citations, in that order.
- "citation" is the [[art:...]] token the number carries, copied exactly, or null when the
  sentence carries none. Do not invent a citation and do not move one from another number.
- "rounding" is the number of decimals the prose wrote when it wrote fewer than the artifact has
  (2 for a lift written 2.24), or null.

Return every number even when it has no citation: a number you leave out is still counted, and
counted against the report.

Prose:
 1| Sensitivity analysis is reported here in the sense that validation should check the effect of changes in inputs and parameter values on model outputs, and should probe behaviour at extreme values to establish the conditions under which a model becomes unstable or inaccurate [[reg:SR11-7:V.1.a]].
 2| 
 3| ### 5.1 Multicollinearity among the retained features
 4| 
 5| Collinearity in the retained feature set was assessed through per-feature variance inflation factors on the training sample and through Belsley's condition number of the column-standardised design.
 6| 
 7| The largest variance inflation factor over the retained features is 7.295 [[art:9ae7c45b:vif.max]], which falls below the declared ceiling of 10 [[art:aeb4f33c:threshold.M1.vif]].
 8| 
 9| That maximum is attained by the six-month mean billed amount at 7.295 [[art:f0a2f865:vif.bill_mean_6m]], with the last payment ratio close behind at 7.264 [[art:c2de8dfe:vif.pay_ratio_last]] and the six-month mean payment ratio at 7.259 [[art:e39c3e82:vif.pay_ratio_mean_6m]].
10| 
11| These three sit together at the top of the range and are mutually close, which is consistent with the billing and payment-ratio constructions sharing much of the same underlying account history.
12| 
13| The credit limit follows at 4.803 [[art:ddfdcc3c:vif.limit_bal]] and utilisation at 3.215 [[art:536fdb6f:vif.utilisation]], both further from the ceiling than the payment-ratio group.
14| 
15| The delinquency features are lower still, at 2.561 [[art:38974def:vif.delinq_count_6m]] for the six-month delinquency count, 2.408 [[art:71aaaf11:vif.delinq_max_6m]] for the six-month maximum and 1.412 [[art:48733638:vif.delinq_last]] for the most recent delinquency.
16| 
17| The six-month billing trend at 1.201 [[art:9356a256:vif.bill_trend_6m]] and age at 1.002 [[art:74c06cad:vif.age]] are the least entangled with the rest of the design, with age near the floor of the statistic.
18| 
19| Belsley's condition number of the column-standardised design is 5.547 [[art:e41b9562:condition_number]], below the declared ceiling of 30 [[art:7e52fd7a:threshold.M1.condition_number]].
20| 
21| Both diagnostics therefore fall on the acceptable side of their declared ceilings, and the condition number in particular indicates no near-degeneracy in the design that would make the fitted coefficients numerically fragile.
22| 
23| The coefficients on the billing and payment-ratio features should nonetheless be read as a group rather than individually, since their variance inflation factors are the largest in the set and are close to one another.
24| 
25| ### 5.2 Analyses that do not apply to this model
26| 
27| The package declares no regime column for this model, so stability of the model across declared regimes is not in scope for this section and is recorded as such in Appendix D.
28| 
29| Nothing below should be read as a regime comparison, and no regime-wise result is reported here.
30| 
31| The subject is not a hazard model, so the rate-shock scenarios are likewise out of scope and are recorded in Appendix D.
32| 
33| This means the value change at the extreme shocks, the monotonicity of the shock curve, and the convexity of that curve against the direction the package declares were not exercises applicable to this model type, and no statement in this section should be read as reporting them.
34| 
35| The sensitivity evidence carried by this section is therefore the collinearity evidence set out above.
36| 
37| Nothing in this section is carried forward as a finding.


Answer with one JSON object and nothing else: no prose before or after it, no explanation, no markdown fence. It must validate against this JSON schema:
{"$defs": {"Comparison": {"description": "What the claimed value is asserted to equal.\n\n``delta`` and ``ratio`` are cited by two adjacent ``[[art:...]]`` tokens, in order (D-012).\nThe enum is not nullable: ``eq`` is the explicit default, so \"this number equals its artifact\"\nhas one spelling and not two (D-018).\n\nAttributes:\n    eq: The value matches the cited artifact.\n    delta: The value matches ``second - first``.\n    ratio: The value matches ``second / first``.", "enum": ["eq", "delta", "ratio"], "title": "Comparison", "type": "string"}, "ExtractedClaim": {"additionalProperties": false, "description": "One claim as the model returns it: the grammar minus the fields the caller already knows.\n\n``text``, ``section``, ``id`` and ``source`` are not asked for. The caller knows which section\nit passed in, the id is a hash of the other three fields, the source of an extraction is\nalways ``report``, and the text is the line the model named -- which the caller has in front\nof it, so asking for it back costs output tokens and adds a way for the answer to disagree\nwith the prose (D-063, D-085).\n\nAttributes:\n    line: The 1-based number of the line the number appears on, as the prompt printed it.\n    value: The number as written, separators and per cent sign removed.\n    unit: How it is written.\n    metric: What it measures, or ``None``.\n    split: Which split it is about, or ``None``.\n    comparison: ``eq``, ``delta`` or ``ratio``.\n    citation: The citation the number carries, or ``None``.\n    rounding: Decimals the prose used, or ``None``.", "properties": {"line": {"minimum": 1, "title": "Line", "type": "integer"}, "value": {"title": "Value", "type": "number"}, "unit": {"$ref": "#/$defs/Unit", "default": "ratio"}, "metric": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "default": null, "title": "Metric"}, "split": {"anyOf": [{"$ref": "#/$defs/SplitName"}, {"type": "null"}], "default": null}, "comparison": {"$ref": "#/$defs/Comparison", "default": "eq"}, "citation": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "default": null, "title": "Citation"}, "rounding": {"anyOf": [{"minimum": 0, "type": "integer"}, {"type": "null"}], "default": null, "title": "Rounding"}}, "required": ["line", "value"], "title": "ExtractedClaim", "type": "object"}, "SplitName": {"description": "The splits a claim may be stated on, exactly as ``CLAIMS_SCHEMA.json`` enumerates them.\n\nAttributes:\n    train: The development split.\n    test: The held-out split.\n    out_of_time: A later-period split; hazard subjects.\n    vintage_holdout: One origination year held out; hazard subjects.", "enum": ["train", "test", "out_of_time", "vintage_holdout"], "title": "SplitName", "type": "string"}, "Unit": {"description": "How a number is written, which decides how it is normalised before matching.\n\nAttributes:\n    ratio: Every dimensionless quantity not written with a ``%`` -- AUC, PSI, VIF, a\n        coefficient, a lift.\n    percent: Written with a ``%``; normalised against a unit-interval artifact by dividing\n        by 100.\n    count: A number of rows, features or events. Matched to half a unit, so integers match\n        exactly.\n    currency: A money amount.\n    bp: Basis points, as a rate shock is written.\n    months: A horizon.", "enum": ["ratio", "percent", "count", "currency", "bp", "months"], "title": "Unit", "type": "string"}}, "additionalProperties": false, "description": "The JSON object the extractor is asked for: a list of claims under one key.\n\nA bare JSON array is a shape more models get wrong than a single-key object, and\n:func:`~quaestor.llm.structured.structured` validates a ``BaseModel``, not a list.\n\nAttributes:\n    claims: The claims, in the order the numbers appear.", "properties": {"claims": {"items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/ExtractedClaim"}, "title": "Claims", "type": "array"}}, "title": "ExtractedClaims", "type": "object"}
